The proposal models distinct load, resource-read, and command operations only as one flat attribute set on the generic `execute_tool` span. Please define `execute_tool` refinements with applicable attributes and span-name formats. These remain `execute_tool` spans, not new span kinds.

This is a working example. It might need polishing and adjustments:

```yaml
span_refinements:
  - id: gen_ai.execute_tool.load_skill.internal
    ref: gen_ai.execute_tool.internal
    brief: Describes a tool call that loads a skill into an agent's context.
    name:
      note: |
        **Span name** SHOULD be `{gen_ai.tool.name} {gen_ai.skill.name}`
        when `gen_ai.skill.name` is available and `{gen_ai.tool.name}`
        otherwise.
    note: |
      This refinement applies when a dedicated tool loads a skill.
      Examples include:

      - [Google ADK](https://adk.dev/skills/) `load_skill`;
      - [OpenAI Agents](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox/guide/)
        `load_skill` for a lazy skill source;
      - [Strands Agents](https://strandsagents.com/docs/user-guide/concepts/plugins/skills/)
        `skills`;
      - [Agno](https://docs.agno.com/skills/overview)
        `get_skill_instructions`.

      Otherwise, the generic `execute_tool` span applies.
    stability: development
    attributes:
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.name
        requirement_level:
          conditionally_required: If the skill name is available.
        sampling_relevant: true
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.description
        requirement_level:
          recommended: If the skill description is available.
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.source.uri
        requirement_level:
          recommended: If the skill source URI is available.

  - id: gen_ai.execute_tool.read_skill_resource.internal
    ref: gen_ai.execute_tool.internal
    brief: Describes a tool call that reads a resource belonging to a skill.
    name:
      note: |
        **Span name** SHOULD be
        `{gen_ai.tool.name} {gen_ai.skill.name} {gen_ai.skill.resource.name}`
        when the skill and resource names are available,
        `{gen_ai.tool.name} {gen_ai.skill.resource.name}` when only the
        resource name is available, and `{gen_ai.tool.name}` otherwise.

        The skill name SHOULD NOT be appended by itself.
    note: |
      This refinement applies when a dedicated tool reads a skill resource.
      Examples include:

      - [Google ADK](https://adk.dev/skills/) `load_skill_resource`;
      - [Microsoft Agent Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/agents/skills)
        `read_skill_resource`;
      - [Agno](https://docs.agno.com/skills/overview)
        `get_skill_reference` and `get_skill_script` when called with
        `execute=false`.

      Otherwise, the generic `execute_tool` span applies.
    stability: development
    attributes:
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.name
        requirement_level:
          conditionally_required: If the skill name is available.
        sampling_relevant: true
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.resource.name
        requirement_level:
          conditionally_required: If the skill resource name is available.
        sampling_relevant: true
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.description
        requirement_level:
          recommended: If the skill description is available.
      - ref: gen_ai.skill.source.uri
        requirement_level:
          recommended: If the skill source URI is available.

  - id: gen_ai.execute_tool.command.internal
    ref: gen_ai.execute_tool.internal
    brief: Describes a tool call that executes one or more commands.
    name:
      note: |
        **Span name** SHOULD be:

        - `{gen_ai.tool.name} {gen_ai.skill.name} {gen_ai.skill.resource.name}`
          when the skill and resource names are both available;
        - `{gen_ai.tool.name} {gen_ai.skill.resource.name}` when only the
          skill resource name is available;
        - `{gen_ai.tool.name} {process.executable.name}` when only the
          executable name is available;
        - `{gen_ai.tool.name}` otherwise.

        The skill name SHOULD NOT be appended without the resource name.
    note: |
      This refinement applies when a tool represents command execution,
      whether or not it is associated with a skill.

      Examples include:

      - [OpenAI Agents](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox/guide/)
        `exec_command`, which runs both general commands and scripts from
        materialized skills;
      - [LangChain Deep Agents](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview)
        sandbox `execute`, which runs both general commands and skill scripts;
      - [Strands Agents](https://strandsagents.com/docs/user-guide/concepts/plugins/skills/)
        `shell`, which is used for both general commands and bundled skill
        scripts;
      - [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool)
        client `bash` for general commands;
      - [Google ADK](https://adk.dev/skills/) `run_skill_script`, which is
        dedicated to scripts bundled with skills;
      - [Agno](https://docs.agno.com/skills/overview) `get_skill_script` when
        called with `execute=true`.

      The tool span covers framework processing such as validation, skill
```
